newsitem.title: UK: UK government says Treasury to regulate insurance.
newsitem.headline: UK government says Treasury to regulate insurance.

text.p: The British government said on Wednesday insurance regulation is to transfer to the Treasury and insurance supervision will, in due course, move to the enhanced Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
Economic Secretary, Helen Liddell, will assume responsibility for insurance regulation.
The widely expected move is part of the government's plans, announced in May, to overhaul financial services regulation in Britain after a series of embarrassing scandals in recent years.
The new regulatory body, dubbed 'super-SIB' will become one of the most powerful of British institutions, regulating banks, securities firms as well as insurance and building societies.
A draft Financial Services Bill, transferring responsibilities for the new body, is expected to be published for consultation in the summer of 1998.
